stem: A client's transferrin saturation is below the laboratory reference interval. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: Less circulating iron is available to occupy transferrin-binding sites, a pattern that can occur with iron deficiency
options.B: The result confirms iron overload because transferrin is highly saturated with iron
options.C: The value is unrelated to iron availability and should not be interpreted with other iron studies
options.D: The result specifically diagnoses vitamin B12 deficiency

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories states that percent transferrin saturation decreases with iron deficiency and increases when iron is in excess. A low saturation therefore reflects reduced iron availability relative to iron-binding capacity and can support iron deficiency when interpreted with ferritin and other iron studies. It is not by itself specific for one diagnosis, particularly in inflammatory conditions. Therefore A is the most accurate interpretation.
educational_objective: Interpret a low transferrin saturation as reduced iron availability that can support iron deficiency when considered with the rest of the iron study profile.
source_version_date: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories test catalog accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Clinical Information: serum iron/TIBC/percent saturation are used in evaluation of iron disorders; percent saturation decreases with iron deficiency and increases when iron is in excess; Interpretation/Cautions: low saturation may screen for iron deficiency but ferritin and other studies improve interpretation, especially with inflammation; Method Description: percent saturation = iron/TIBC ×100
source_claim_supported: Transferrin saturation decreases when iron availability is reduced, including iron deficiency, and should be interpreted with other iron studies rather than treated as a diagnosis by itself.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential: interpret diagnostic and laboratory test results and recognize abnormal findings requiring follow-up
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — laboratory interpretation / transferrin saturation
correction_summary: Upgraded the source to Mayo Clinic Laboratories and removed the padded colleague narrative. Avoided treating a low transferrin saturation as uniquely diagnostic of iron deficiency, because low iron availability can also occur in inflammatory/chronic-disease contexts. No universal numeric threshold was inserted into the item.
audit_findings: A is the only option that accurately describes what low transferrin saturation represents without overdiagnosis. B reverses the direction of the result; C ignores its role in iron studies; D assigns an unrelated specific deficiency. The inflammatory-disease caveat is preserved, eliminating second-answer and overprecision risk.
